title: Top Gear is back in 2028, with chef Gordon Ramsay at the wheel
summary: Rev up those engines — the British show that sparked the now globally-successful Top Gear franchise is returning, with celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay at the wheel as its new main presenter.

image.caption: Celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay is the new presenter of the British motoring show Top Gear, which will be returning with new episodes in 2028, according to the BBC. (BBC Top Gear Magazine)

blocks.text: Rev up those engines — the British show that sparked the now globally-successful Top Gear franchise is returning, with celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay at the wheel as its new main presenter.
Show returning 4 years after previous host Andrew 'Freddie' Flintoff's serious crash
Yes, the man who came to fame whipping up high-end food and yelling at hapless would-be-chefs in shows like MasterChef and Hell's Kitchen is now trading in his cooking knives for car keys.

In a video announcing Top Gear's return, Ramsay holds on for dear life in the passenger seat of a sports car as it careens down a track at top speed, the show's eternally-helmeted, iconic stunt driver The Stig in the driver's seat.
"Top Gear is back," Ramsay exclaims over the sound of the engine.

The show has been off the air in the U.K. since previous presenter Andrew 'Freddie' Flintoff suffered serious injuries in a crash on Top Gear's test track during filming in 2023. A safety review was carried out in the months following the crash, but the BBC decided at the time to park the show "for the foreseeable future."
The future, it seems, is here. The show will begin filming next year and will start airing episodes in the U.K. in 2028, according to the BBC.
Ramsay may be better known for his skills in the kitchen, but he has always been a car fan, he said in a BBC Top Gear magazine article announcing his casting.

“My love affair with cars began as a child, growing up a field away from Silverstone, where I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing,” Ramsay said. “That early excitement sparked a lifelong passion for cars, motorsport, beautiful design and extraordinary engineering."
In the new series, Ramsay will be joined by a team of as-yet-unrevealed co-presenters and filming will include "locations across the globe," the BBC stated.

items: BBC parks popular Top Gear show after presenter injured

blocks.text: Top Gear is an enduring British show, stretching back to a 1977 show under the BBC. The modern version of the show, which has inspired international formats and spinoffs, started in 2002 and included reviews of cars, vehicular challenges, races and a popular celebrity segment in which celebrity guests competed to set the fastest lap on the Top Gear track.

Ramsay himself has appeared on the show as a guest three times before. The BBC noted that he "once managed to hustle a Chevy Lacetti around the TG Test Track in 1m 46.3s," during the Star in a Reasonably-Priced Car segment, calling him "a dab hand at the track."
The crash that brought Top Gear to a halt wasn't the first time the British show made headlines.

The show fired original co-presenter Jeremy Clarkson — a controversial figure whose bluster helped the show initially find success — in 2015, following a physical altercation with a producer. Clarkson, who had previously been disciplined for allegedly using a racial slur on set, publicly apologized to producer Oisin Tymon in 2016 after Tymon sued for personal injury and racial discrimination.

Following Clarkson's ousting, the show rattled through a roster of co-presenters, including Chris Evans (not that one), Matt LeBlanc and Rory Reid. In 2019, Flintoff took over as main presenter alongside Chris Harris and Paddy McGuinness.
